prize_parts.citation: for a body of fiction in which dream logic dissolves ordinary psychology, space and causality, and renews narrative perception in modern Chinese literature

statement.case_for: My opening view holds after reading my colleagues' arguments. The case for Can Xue rests on the oeuvre, not on a single title. Her fiction (e.g. Frontier; Love in the New Millennium) offers a voice that is hard to mistake for anyone else's. Its dream logic is a rigorously kept formal principle, not a decorative device. It replaces conventional psychology and causal plot with a different way of constructing a narrative world, which meets the criteria of distinctiveness of voice and formal achievement. Her critical writing on Western and Chinese literature adds intellectual depth, so the project is reflective as well as imaginative. The oeuvre has been pursued consistently over several decades, which supports maturity. A single-writer citation is unproblematic because the contribution is one personal fictional method, with few close analogues in Chinese or world literature. I weigh this on literary grounds alone and take no account of nationality, language or symbolism. I note that the other opening assessments describe the same strengths independently, but I treat that as a cross-check on my reading and not as evidence of merit.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is that the method is very consistent, and it is unclear whether consistency here means sustained invention or repetition across a large body of stories and novels. Her prose is also read largely in translation, and its abstract, dense texture may lose much in transit. Only part of the corpus is available to readers outside Chinese, so the judgment of sustained quality is partly indirect. I have not independently verified the full corpus or the quality of the translations. If the committee concluded that the long works do not sustain the invention of the best short fiction, the case would weaken considerably.

responses.point: Mattson ranks Cărtărescu first for a recognizable visionary voice, large-scale dense prose built from body, memory and metaphysical speculation, and coherence across prose and poetry. She also asks whether Can Xue's method evolves or only repeats itself.
responses.response: I accept the strength of the Cărtărescu case and placed him third on similar grounds: unmistakable voice, imaginative scale, a rooting in Romanian tradition. Her question about Can Xue is fair and I cannot answer it conclusively from the supplied description. Where I differ is on the risk. Cărtărescu's density and possible repetition over very long volumes seem to me a comparable concern to the one she raises about Can Xue, so it does not clearly separate them. What persuades me is that Can Xue's formal discipline appears to be the work itself, while Cărtărescu's achievement leans more on accumulation and lineage. That is a judgment, not a verified finding, and both depend on translators. I would keep Cărtărescu as my first alternative and would not resist a committee reading that rates his long novels higher.

responses.point: Olsson ranks Zurita first. He sees long poetic sequences (Purgatory, Anteparadise) that turn collective suffering under dictatorship into memorial form, and a poetry extended into landscape-scale gestures, with the case resting on the poetry and not on political symbolism.
responses.response: I take the formal ambition seriously and agree with him that the claim must rest on the poems' language and structure, not on historical weight. That is why I ranked Zurita fifth and not lower. Two things hold me back. First, poetry is the genre hardest to judge in translation, and non-Spanish readers depend heavily on translators for the very qualities in question. Second, the non-textual interventions are a real open question under the framework of Nobel's will, and Olsson himself says they should be treated as context. If the poems alone carry the case, I would want that shown against the translated texts. I cannot show it. Zurita is therefore not among my alternatives, but I would revisit this if the committee can show how the sequences hold up as literature on the page.

responses.point: Sward ranks Can Xue first for sentence-level and structural invention in a long, formally consistent body of work, and Marilynne Robinson second for meditative, morally serious prose, while noting that Robinson's fiction is thematically narrow and compact.
responses.response: Her reading of Can Xue matches mine, including her caution that formal monotony cannot be settled from the supplied description. On Robinson I agree about the sentence-level control and the rereadability of Housekeeping and the Gilead novels. I ranked her sixth because of the compact fiction output, which she names herself as a limit on breadth. The essays extend the project but do not obviously enlarge the formal range. I would not claim that a small oeuvre is disqualifying. My reservation is only that, under the common criteria, the breadth of sustained achievement looks narrower than in the candidates I rank higher, and I have not verified critical consensus on the later Gilead volumes.

uncertainties: How much of Can Xue's large output of stories and novels is available in translation, and how well the translations convey the texture of the Chinese prose; I have not independently verified this.
Whether the consistency of her method amounts to sustained invention over the whole oeuvre or to repetition; this cannot be settled from the supplied description.

How Adonis should be compared with the prose candidates. His case rests on Arabic prosody and poetic language that I cannot judge from translation, and I rely on critical reputation more than on direct reading.
Whether Cărtărescu's long novels sustain their density without repetition across their full length.

statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile. Her biography, journalism and Academy role show no documented tie to any shortlisted writer. Her marriage to Pär Nuder and her work on Nobel and Wallenberg biographies have no evident link to the candidates. Her own non-fiction practice is context and not evidence for or against any candidate.
